findings.highlight: You don't know unless you try!
findings.evidenceJa: “弾いてみなきゃわからない”って言われてるみたいで
findings.explanation: Kazusa dislikes an evaluation implying that nobody knows how well she will perform until she actually plays—an accusation of inconsistency. Todokanai TL turns it into the generic encouragement 'you don't know unless you try,' reversing criticism into motivational advice and weakening Youko's demand for stability.
findings.japanese:
「いちピアニストとしてはその評価はあまり嬉しくないな。
“弾いてみなきゃわからない”って言われてるみたいで」
findings.todokanai: "Being a pianist, I can't say that evaluation makes me happy. It's like you're telling me 'You don't know unless you try!' or something."

findings.highlight: provide me with such incredible power
findings.evidenceJa: そんな練習環境を用意できるなら、是非とも頼むよ社長
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks her boss to provide a training environment in which fifty or one hundred hours of daily practice are possible, setting up the Hyperbolic Time Chamber joke. Todokanai TL asks for 'incredible power,' breaking the transition from impossible hours to a time-altering room.
findings.japanese:
「そんな練習環境を用意できるなら、
是非とも頼むよ社長」
findings.todokanai: "If you can provide me with such incredible power, then by all means, boss."

findings.highlight: join me in my critique of these mandarins
findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんとボケに乗ってくれないと困るのよねぇ
findings.explanation: Youko complains that Kazusa failed to play along with her comic bit, which deliberately diverted the apology into frozen-mandarin expertise. Todokanai TL calls this a sincere critique of the fruit, deleting the joke-versus-seriousness contrast.
findings.japanese: 「…ちゃんとボケに乗ってくれないと困るのよねぇ」
findings.todokanai: "…I was really hoping you'd join me in my critique of these mandarins."

findings.evidenceJa: 母さんも、日本での用事を済ませてウィーンに帰ってきた
findings.explanation: Youko finished what business she could in Japan and returned to Vienna one week after Kazusa fled. 'Also left' omits the destination and the return that begins the passage about Youko abandoning Japan to follow and protect her daughter.
findings.japanese: 母さんも、日本での用事を済ませてウィーンに帰ってきた。
findings.todokanai: After finishing up the last of her business, Mom also left.

findings.highlight: my emotions were a mix of despair, unease and grief.
findings.evidenceJa: その事実に今さら納得してしまう自分がいた
findings.explanation: Amid despair, agitation, and grief, Kazusa recognizes that part of her is belatedly convinced by the truth of Youko's illness. Todokanai TL stops at the emotional mixture and omits the dawning acceptance that makes the next two explanations suddenly fit.
findings.japanese:
ウィーンで最初にその事実を知ったとき、
絶望や焦燥や悲嘆が混ざりあう感情の片隅で、
その事実に今さら納得してしまう自分がいた。
findings.todokanai: When I first found out about the truth, here in Vienna, my emotions were a mix of despair, unease and grief.

findings.highlight: I lost the little love I had for the idiotic daughter
findings.evidenceJa: 馬鹿娘に愛想が尽きた
findings.explanation: Kazusa is the foolish daughter and becomes disgusted with herself for trampling her mother's grave resolve over a childish heartbreak. Todokanai TL speaks as though she were a separate observer who possessed only a little love for that daughter, distorting both person and emotional direction.
findings.japanese:
そんな母親の重い決意を、
子供みたいな失恋で踏みにじってしまった
馬鹿娘に愛想が尽きた。
findings.todokanai: I lost the little love I had for the idiotic daughter who trampled all over her mother's determination, all because of some childish heartbreak.

findings.evidenceJa: 骨髄移植したらかなりの確率で治るんだろ？それに親族の方が適合する確率高いんだろ？
findings.explanation: Kazusa argues that a bone-marrow transplant has a strong chance of curing Youko and that relatives are more likely to match. Todokanai TL drops both medical premises and leaves only the insult, so Youko's 'And so what?' no longer answers a translated argument.
findings.japanese:
「馬鹿なのはそっちだろ！
骨髄移植したらかなりの確率で治るんだろ？
それに親族の方が適合する確率高いんだろ？」

findings.highlight: All because I've had a lifetime's worth of happiness…
findings.evidenceJa: 一生分の望みを叶えてしまったせいで…天国を垣間見てしまったせいで、今までよりも、過酷な現実が
findings.explanation: Because Kazusa fulfilled a lifetime's wishes and glimpsed heaven, the continuing reality is harsher than ever before. Todokanai TL reduces wishes to generic happiness, omits the glimpse of heaven, and leaves the causal literary climax incomplete.
findings.japanese:
一生分の望みを叶えてしまったせいで…
天国を垣間見てしまったせいで、
今までよりも、過酷な現実が。
findings.todokanai: A reality cruel beyond anything that preceded it. All because I've had a lifetime's worth of happiness…
